Round one gave 4 with no admission that only direct ones were listed; this is now correct and discloses direct vs transitive.

findings: Fixed and verified: the three override cases (MailHandler/ElasticaHandler handleBatch, SocketHandler close) are no longer high; the edges are now low and the reason says which descendants redeclare the method. The target is still the base-class method, so they remain wrong-but-hedged edges (2 of the 30 in my low sample are such cases: RotatingFileHandler::close and LogMonsterHandler::close).
Fixed and verified: PHPUnit mock-builder with()/expects() calls bind to nothing (0 test edges to LogRecord::with); all four round-one cases are gone.
Fixed and verified: find_implementations HandlerInterface lists transitively (69 = true count) and says how many are direct (4); the first line now also states the truncation.

Hierarchy defect: `extends \DateTimeImmutable` (global built-in) in JsonSerializableDateTimeImmutable.php is bound to the repo's own Monolog\DateTimeImmutable (EXTENDS medium), which is circular since that class extends it; the leading backslash is not honoured. In the 20-edge sample this is 1 wrong (round one 0 of 20).

A Gelf\Message->toArray() call (type proven by assertInstanceOf) is bound at low to LogRecord::toArray: external-type method name collisions still produce low-tier wrong edges (1 of 30), as does an anonymous-class boom() -> TestInternalFrame::boom (round one's case, unchanged).

Fluent chains on $this (SlackRecord constructor) still lose 6 of 8 calls to ambiguity (setUsername, useAttachment, ... have no edge), and $handler->isHandling($record) in Logger::addRecord (a HandlerInterface element) has no edge; unchanged.
Hierarchy edges remain mostly medium/low (211 of 238) even for same-namespace supertypes, so verdicts say 'mixed' although the targets are right (19 of 20).
The new 'may be passed as a value' evidence on find_callers/analyze_impact cites README.md and doc/*.md (calls in documentation), not code: over-cautious.
